newsitem.title: UK: U.S, Japan funds to sell own equity markets-Merrill.
newsitem.headline: U.S, Japan funds to sell own equity markets-Merrill.

text.p: U.S. and Japanese fund managers expect to be sellers of their own equity markets at the start of 1997, while both they and Continental European funds expect buouyant equity markets in Europe, according to Merrill Lynch.

The Merrill survey, which covered 46 U.S. money managers with $1.7 trillion under management, 41 Japanese institutions managing $688 billion and 67 Continental European institutions managing $677 billion, showed all were keener on cash holdings.
Among U.S. funds, a balance of 20 percent expected to be sellers of their domestic equity market after a balance of 12 percent being sellers in December.

"In the U.S., only a third of investors are projecting a higher growth rate over the coming year. This bearishness on growth is reflected in the asset allocation with managers looking to buy Treasuries and reduce their holdings of U.S. equities," said Merrill global strategist Bijal Shah.
The balance is the difference between those planning to increase their allocations and those looking to cut.
By sector, the survey showed investors favour financials and technology, with the least favoured area building cyclicals.
A balance of 11 percent of the U.S. funds questioned said they planned to raise their exposure to U.S. Treasuries after a positive balance of two percent in December.
"U.S. fund managers are very good judges of value in the Treasury market," said Merrill's Shah.
Another favoured area is emerging markets, with a balance of 22 percent looking to raise exposure to Latin America and 37 percent wanting to increase holdings of Pacific Basin equiies.
"Looking at short term money rates fund managers do not see much risk in higher interest rates and are pushing money into emerging markets," Shah noted.
U.S. funds are also raising cash, with a balance of seven percent planning to increase cash holdings after four percent in December and eight percent in November.
The Japanese equity market remains unloved both by U.S. fund managers, and more importantly by domestic Japanese investors.
A balance of two percent are sellers of a market which plunged to a 17-month low with a loss of 2,057 points last week.
Merrill's Shah said the correlation between Japanese money managers and market performance has been close.
They are keen on continental European markets, with a balance of 17 percent looking to increase exposure after a positive seven percent in December.
Among fixed income markets, Japanese funds are slowing their sales of domestic bonds and fewer, 10 percent versus 21 percent in December, are looking to increase holdings of overseas bonds.
A balance of two percent are looking to reduce cash after seven percent last month.
Among continental European equities, which are favoured by fund managers from the U.S., Japan and Britain and Europe, fund managers favour growth stocks, especially pharmaceuticals.
"We are at the early stages of recovery in Europe and interest rates are not expected to go higher," said Shah.
Of the a balance of 27 percent expect to raise exposure to equities in the region, while a balance of 24 percent are looking to sell European bonds.
They are also raising cash aggressively, a balance of 24 percent are looking to increase holdings and Shah believes that most of this is being financed by sales of bonds.

Bears on the German bond market outnumber bulls by a balance of 59 percent, while 83 percent are bullish on the German stockmarket and 17 percent on the French stockmarket. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
